messages:
Anya: Quick sync — proposal for a 'windowed preheat' pattern for deploy-time warmers. Instead of firing a single large burst at deploy, we spread many small micro-warmers across staggered windows per shard to: reduce KV eviction spikes, avoid batch-size-induced kernel fallbacks, and smooth outgoing RPS during autoscale transitions. Thoughts?

Matt: Curious — how do we pick window boundaries? per-shard hash, or per-host?

Anya: Per-shard (hash of prefix key modulo N_windows) + a small jitter. Example: shard_count=64, windows=6, jitter=0-15s. That keeps any one host from seeing >1/win of the total warmers. Pseudoconfig: ```yaml
warmers:
  windows: 6
  jitter_s: 15
  probe_ttl: 30m
  per_window_qps: 5
```

Jia: fyi from profiling yesterday — when we moved to a single big burst, host CPU sched increased and kernel selection flipped to a fallback path for long sequences. Small bursts preserved the preferred kernel. I can paste the flamegraph if useful.

Sam: Noted regression: large bursts pushed batch_size into big-batched path which triggers a slower attention kernel on some GPUs (see logs). We need a guard that caps batch growth during warmers to avoid changing the kernel selection metric. Suggested flag: `--max-warm-batch=16`.

Leo: Also watch KV curb churn. If the warmers touch high-card keys across hosts, we see cross-host evictions. We should prefer warmers that use stable prefixes (user-id-ish) rather than randomized top-level keys. Idea: warm by representative prefix + small suffix probe.

Anya: Agree. Proposal: two-tier probe keying — (1) canonical prefix set from production telemetry, (2) suffix entropy limited to 8 bits for coverage. That reduces unique key cardinality while still exercising KV locality.

Jia: Quick data snapshot from last run (post-change):
`windowed run: hit_rate=0.74, host_eviction_rate=0.02, avg_latency_p95=112ms`
`single-burst run: hit_rate=0.58, host_eviction_rate=0.11, avg_latency_p95=170ms`
Small sample but promising.

Sam: One more corner: autoscaler scale-up events — when new hosts come up, we sometimes run a full re-seed that collides with scheduled warmers and creates a net >1 burst. Need coordination: prewarm for new hosts should be on a separate, lower-rate channel and respect global in-flight warmers counter.

Anya: Good catch. Add an autoscale backoff: newly provisioned hosts receive a reduced preheat rate for first 10 minutes and join the window schedule at a random offset. Config snippet: ```json
{"autoscale_preheat": {"rate_factor": 0.25, "ramp_minutes": 10}}
```

Leo: Also add a global soft limiter (token-bucket) so scheduled jobs and deploy warmers share capacity. Prevents runaway during multi-cluster rollouts.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: `preheat-orchestrator/v2` queued at 2026-03-18T14:20Z :gear:

Anya: Action items:
- Jia: run a 24h A/B comparing canonical-prefix keying vs suffix-random (start tonight)
- Sam: add `--max-warm-batch` guard and autoscale rate_factor enforcement (PR)
- Leo: implement global token-bucket limiter in orchestration service
- Matt: sanity-check kernel selection telemetry to ensure warmers don't flip paths

Anya: If no objections I'll roll this out to canary cluster tomorrow morning with windows=6 and per_window_qps=5. :thumbsup:

Matt: :+1: go ahead on canary.

Jia: I'll post flamegraphs to the thread after the run.

Sam: ACK, starting work on guards.

Leo: ACK, will prototype limiter.

Anya: thanks all — will update deploy ticket with these params.
